threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of just 'the Overground' for your local journeys. Everyone here knows the real magic is above ground.
Caught a guy singing opera at the back of the 196 last night. Only in Brixton does that feel normal—everyone joined in for a verse.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids playing football in the street, their laughter mixing with the sound of the nearby kebab shop’s grill. That was Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a silent disco in a former factory, where the beats blend with the sound of the Spree — surreal but so local.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how easily they navigate around BART delays—while newcomers just stare at the screen like it’ll start moving on its own.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The Muni bus rolled up with a guy playing a saxophone out front, and between stops, he even took requests. Classic San Francisco hustle.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the flower shops sell the same stuff, but locals know the ones with unique plants are hidden in backstreets like Carrer de Verdi.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they order 'tapas' as if it's a single dish. Locals know it's a sharing experience, not a meal.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can get a seat on the bus during rush hour. Good luck with that—it's standing room only, at best.
Caught a glimpse of a guy in full tuxedo arguing with a traffic cone outside the Ritzy. Only in Brixton, right? The night bus crew had a good laugh.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a street musician serenading a group of kids while their parents argued over the price of falafel at the stand nearby.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous, pop-up kiez parties spilling onto the streets, complete with rooftop DJs and locals cooking up Currywurst for everyone.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local when they confidently navigate the BART delays and still manage to grab a burrito before the next train. It's an art.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo hop on the 47, clutching a bouquet. Muni’s always the backdrop for spontaneous moments in this city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just grab a 'café con leche' everywhere, but around here, it's all about the 'tallat'—and it's way better.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll notice them awkwardly trying to navigate the narrow streets, constantly checking maps instead of just following the crowd.
